question: Can reusing errors seen in the actual training forward improve functional-graph adaptation at lower cost than a separate diagnostic sweep?
objective: Unchanged rank-eight block and shared readout. Mean CE over six categorical states per map and then across eight maps. Fresh AdamW for each branch, retain moments across both cycles.
distribution: Uniform independent eight-state successor maps; one frozen randomized symbolic presentation per map. Same fresh batches in both arms. One independent development cohort. Anchor retention on 96 historical random0 permissioned development permutations at three hops.
selection: Within each cycle take one unique replay example from each consecutive stratum of three fresh maps (32 strata, no replacement). Static uses a preseeded independent uniform choice within each stratum. Online uses pre-update correct-prefix length from its own fresh forward. Prefer an intermediate prefix of 1..5 nearest to three for strata 0,1,2 modulo five; for stratum 3 prefer lowest prefix; for stratum 4 highest prefix. Break ties by a seeded hash of map ID. Replay selected maps in stratum order. No extra candidate inference.
gate: At the second endpoint require >=3 percentage points online minus static sixth-hop accuracy and <=2 percentage points online third-hop permutation retention loss versus parent. Stop after matched round one if either loses >5 absolute points on the 96-map permutation anchor. Charge rollout, training and selection; optional measured-time static only if equal-update gate passes.
execution_change: Fresh fair forks from same registered parent, same map sets and selections. Padded position cap 84 after registered cap 384 encountered system pressure at update six. Include 17.38s failed workload in study cost. Stop on recurrence of pressure.
